facts.raw_span: A woman in her 60s presented with a 3-month history of pain, swelling, and erythema on her face
left breast carcinoma diagnosed eleven years earlier
treated with mastectomy, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy
left supraclavicular lymph nodes metastasis treated with surgical excision
pain on palpation
no fever or chills
Violaceous swelling with telangiectasia and necrosis on the forehead, eyelids, nose, and cheek, predominantly involving the left side of the face
Hyperkeratosis, epidermal atrophy, and dilated vessels in the dermis
nests of highly atypical cells
Epithelial cells in the dilated vessels were positive for CD31
atypical cells were strongly positive for GATA3
Telangiectatic, swelling erythema mainly involving the left side of the forehead, eyelids, nose, and cheek

concepts.why: The patient has a history of left breast carcinoma with metastasis, and the current symptoms and histopathological examination show nests of highly atypical cells positive for GATA3, which is consistent with cutaneous metastasis of breast carcinoma.
The patient's symptoms and histopathological examination show telangiectatic swelling, dilated vessels, and nests of highly atypical cells, which are consistent with angiosarcoma.

The patient has a history of breast carcinoma with lymph node metastasis, and the current symptoms show telangiectatic swelling and nests of highly atypical cells, which are consistent with Stewart-Treves syndrome.

rationales.F02: History of breast carcinoma increases likelihood of cutaneous metastasis.
rationales.F09: Presence of highly atypical cells suggests malignancy, consistent with both cutaneous metastasis and angiosarcoma.
rationales.F11: GATA3 positivity is strongly associated with breast carcinoma, supporting cutaneous metastasis and ruling out angiosarcoma.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's history of left breast carcinoma and metastasis, combined with the presence of highly atypical cells in the dermis and strong positivity for GATA3, supports cutaneous metastasis of breast carcinoma as the most likely diagnosis.
